title: Effects of prolonged ethanol intake: production of fatty liver despite adequate diets
authors: Lieber CS, Jones DP, DeCarli LM
population: Five people aged 36 to 62 years, four of them men, with a history of alcoholism and of biopsy-proven alcoholic fatty liver, abstinent and with normal liver morphology at entry; pair-fed rats
funder: Supported in part by the U. S. Army Medical Research and Development Command, Department of the Army contract DA-49-193-MD-2013, and U. S. Public Health Service research grant AM 06284 from the National Institute of Arthritis and Metabolic Diseases. Lieber held a U. S. Public Health Service Research Career Development Award.
result: Under metabolic ward conditions, isocaloric substitution of ethanol for carbohydrate in an adequate diet, or addition of ethanol (up to 300 g per day) to it, produced fat accumulation in liver biopsies of all five subjects. In rats given 36% of energy as ethanol for 24 days, hepatic triglycerides were 89.4 mg/g against 11.3 mg/g in pair-fed controls (19 pairs); replacing the same carbohydrate with fat produced no fatty liver.
